key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst, paired with microalgae as a sacrificial carbon-negative scavenger, substantially boosts solar-driven CO2-to-CO/CH4 conversion.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a scalable materials-and-process strategy for improving photocatalytic carbon conversion while simultaneously leveraging a biologically renewable feedstock.
method: Use bi-polymorphy (layered perovskite + pyrochlore) to support charge transport and surface activity
Compare CO2 reduction performance with no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using microalgae increases CO production by 10× and CH4 production by 4× relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: Microalgae handling, separation, and reaction-condition control may complicate real-world implementation and must be validated for long-term stability.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
